result.summary: This clip opens in the middle of a close call with a jaguar and then moves into jaguar facts, with dramatic black-and-white close-ups and bold keyword text. Compared with the three most-viewed reference Shorts, the biggest gaps are that captions are turned off, there are spoken stumbles in the fact section, and the clip ends mid-sentence. Like Rosolie's own 'Amazon's Jaguar tracks' clip, it runs about 100 seconds, so tightening it matters.
strengths: The cold open drops you straight into the camera-trap story. That matches how all three references start in the middle of an anecdote.
The extreme close-ups of the jaguar's eyes and teeth match lines like 'Tongue out, big teeth out' and make the close call feel real.

suggestions.title: Turn on word-by-word highlighted captions
suggestions.text: Captions are currently disabled. Turn on word-by-word captions with bold text and highlight key words like 'JAGUAR', 'TEETH' and 'BITE FORCE', the way 'Midges are SO tiny...' and 'His Dog Only Bites With No Witnesses' do.
suggestions.reason: Viewers could follow the whole conversation with the sound off, not just the few keyword overlays.

suggestions.title: Start on 'One time' instead of 'Or'
suggestions.text: Trim the opening 'Or' so the first word is 'One time I was checking a camera trap.' 'Paul Rosolie: The Amazon's Jaguar tracks' opens on a clean, complete line (the guide's warning), and this clip should too.
suggestions.reason: The first sentence will sound like a deliberate start instead of a clip cut out of the middle of a thought.

suggestions.title: Cut stumbles in the fact section
suggestions.text: Remove false starts like 'They are... The Jags... Okay. So the Jags are...' (around 62.8s), 'There's one old old...' (around 39.4s) and 'The... With big cats, they usually...' (around 45.2s). 'His Dog Only Bites With No Witnesses' is fast-cut, with 13 cuts in 45 seconds.
suggestions.reason: The second half would keep the same momentum as the opening story instead of slowing down.

suggestions.title: Tighten pauses around the jaguar reveal
suggestions.text: Shorten the roughly one-second gaps after 'one of my friend' (14.5s) and before 'Looked at me' (21.2s). Keep only a short beat before 'The jag just walked by.' The references are mostly continuous speech, with few gaps of silence.
suggestions.reason: The reveal hits harder and the story gets to the payoff sooner.

suggestions.title: Add labeled jaguar-versus-leopard comparison
suggestions.text: While he compares stocky jaguars with lean leopards, overlay a side-by-side image with labels. 'Midges are SO tiny...' does this with a labeled midge-vs-mosquito image.
suggestions.reason: Viewers can see the size and build difference he's describing instead of only hearing it.

suggestions.title: Keep any music well under the voice
suggestions.text: If there's a dramatic music bed, duck it during the story beat 'The jag just walked by' and keep the voice in front. None of the three references has noticeable music; they rely on clear, forward conversation.
suggestions.reason: Dialogue is what carries this story, so keeping it clear protects the suspense.
